stories.headline: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on its site
stories.blurb: Meta's Muse AI agent can no longer buy things on Amazon after the retailer cut it off over the weekend. Users now see a popup saying the 'unauthorized AI agent' violates Amazon's terms of service. Meta apparently didn't tell Amazon it was building a shopping agent that would crawl their site.
stories.why_it_matters: The first major AI agent turf war just started — and it's over who controls your shopping data.
stories.original_headline: Amazon blocks Meta’s Muse AI agent

stories.headline: Google's first laptops start at $899 with built-in AI
stories.blurb: Google announced pricing for its first 'Googlebooks' laptops, made by Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, and ASUS. Starting at $899, the laptops come with built-in AI features and mark Google's entry into the high-end laptop market where AI capabilities are now standard.
stories.why_it_matters: Google is competing directly with Windows and Mac laptops in premium hardware for the first time.
stories.original_headline: Google Rolls Out $899-Plus Googlebooks from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, ASUS

stories.headline: Anthropic files for IPO while its CEO warns against racing to AGI
stories.blurb: The company behind Claude is going public with $100 billion in annualized revenue, even as CEO Dario Amodei publicly argues that some advanced AI models should slow down. The IPO prospectus acknowledges safety risks while betting investors will fund exactly the kind of scale-up Amodei has cautioned against.
stories.why_it_matters: A company can warn about AI risks and still ask Wall Street to fund the race.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic Pursues IPO Despite Its A.I. Safety Warnings

stories.headline: Legal AI startup Harvey is ditching OpenAI to cut its inference bill
stories.blurb: Harvey, the $15.6 billion legal AI company, is moving away from GPT-4 and other closed models because inference costs got too high. The company built its business on fine-tuning OpenAI's models for lawyers, but soaring AI bills are pushing it toward open-source alternatives it can run itself.
stories.why_it_matters: When your AI costs eat your margins, you stop renting and start hosting
stories.original_headline: Startups Like Harvey Embrace Open Models to Cut Reliance on Anthropic, OpenAI
